framework: US NIST AI RMF Playbook (AIRC; companion to AI RMF 1.0)
requirement_paraphrase: Suggested actions include testing and evaluating systems in non-optimised conditions, measuring systems before deployment in conditions similar to expected scenarios, measuring validity (false positive/negative rates) and efficiency against ground truth in deployment context, and documenting differences between measurement setting and deployment environment.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Annexure C (AI Ethics Checklist), approx. pp. 41-46; layout scrambled in extraction, low confidence
requirement_paraphrase: Provides a lifecycle checklist (Plan and Design, Prepare Input Data, Build and Validate, Deploy and Monitor) with a column marking whether each item is binding for third parties.

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
clause_or_page: s3.8.2.2 body text, p.42 (heading concerns an oversight mechanism for data)
requirement_paraphrase: Privacy impact assessments should be conducted and also cover societal and ethical considerations.

framework: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 (PDPL)
requirement_paraphrase: Before processing that uses modern technologies and poses a high risk to privacy and confidentiality, the controller must assess the impact of the planned processing. Mandatory cases include systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects by automated processing (including profiling) with legal or serious effects, and large-scale processing of sensitive data. Minimum content: description and purpose, necessity and suitability, privacy risk assessment, and mitigation measures.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Content red teaming probes the app dynamically for blind spots, multi-turn failures and subjective harms; define targeted vs open-ended objectives; use domain experts, AI experts and target end users with diversity; track acceptable response rate, refusal rate and turns-to-unsafe; annotators may be red teamers, independent third parties or LLM judges with human sampling; automated red teaming (e.g. PAIR, Crescendo-style) is an emerging complement.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories obtain assurance that security mitigations meet the Security Goal through independent external security reviews where internal expertise is inadequate, frequent red-teaming of network and physical access management, competitive bug bounties for public-facing endpoints, periodic personnel integrity testing, third-party security reporting channels, endpoint/intrusion detection tools and a security incident response team.

framework: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 (PDPL)
requirement_paraphrase: The controller must periodically review the outcomes of the impact assessment where the level of risk changes.

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends AI-specific penetration testing of AI system components before deployment and periodically afterwards, including testing outputs and system behaviour.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Check robustness (varied, perturbed, adversarial phrasing) and consistency (repeat runs); test breadth and depth scaled to stakes, repeating tests and evaluating average, minimum and maximum scores; if resources are limited, either use a subset instead of full benchmarks, or run the full set once and repeat a targeted subset (e.g. borderline prompts).

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems informing critical decisions should be subject to appropriate external audit; publishing the results should be considered.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Self-Assessment tool (National Data Governance Platform service)
requirement_paraphrase: Tool for entities to compare their current practice against defined standards and obtain the level of ethical compliance of an AI model; links to the AI Ethics Principles.

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
requirement_paraphrase: AISI states it tests leading AI systems before they are released and collaborates with AI companies, with pre-deployment access to leading models; it open-sources evaluation tools such as Inspect.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories define measurable systemic risk tiers or other acceptance criteria and proceed with development, release or use only if systemic risks are determined acceptable; otherwise they restrict, withdraw or recall and add mitigations.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Consider baseline benchmark performance when selecting a model; evaluate capability claims with empirically validated methods; share pre-deployment test results with actors holding release approval authority; use a purpose-built testing environment such as NIST Dioptra.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.5.2, printed p.15; Implementation Guidance 3.5.2 (Defending Against AI/ML Attacks), printed p.38
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must deploy comprehensive defences for AI/ML systems including continuous monitoring and regular testing. Guidance: regular security testing, including penetration testing and red-teaming exercises, should be run on AI/ML systems to find weaknesses; defensive techniques (e.g. adversarial training) should be built in during development and deployment.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 7.2 / Process 7.2.1, p.72 (technical testing, generative AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Test for safety and possible harms against individuals or groups using benchmarks and red-teaming, document red-teamer instructions, and have stakeholders judge score acceptability.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Compare results with pre-defined thresholds then review failure cases; adjust thresholds only with documented evidence; break results down by sub-category and attack technique, quantify variance and confidence intervals across runs, and analyse failures qualitatively including faults in the LLM judge.

framework: Japan - Guideline for Ensuring Appropriateness of AI R&D and Utilization (decided 19 Dec 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators are to identify and evaluate misuse risks (cyberattacks, fraud) and apply current techniques to reduce inappropriate outputs and malfunction.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
clause_or_page: Overview table p.7; Part 3 step 2 sections 3.2-3.6 (starting pp.37, 52, 62, 73, 82)
requirement_paraphrase: Prescribes risk-specific tests: hallucination (domain knowledge, out-of-domain handling, RAG); bias (parity and counterfactual perturbation tests); undesirable content (type, ease of elicitation, helpfulness/over-refusal); data leakage (type of data, elicitation, system prompt); adversarial prompts (direct and indirect injection).

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Avoid extrapolating performance from narrow or anecdotal assessments; review and verify sources and citations in outputs during pre-deployment measurement and monitoring; regularly review safety/security guardrails, including reasons the system was initially judged safe to deploy.

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: When a vulnerability is detected, disable or restrict vulnerable AI features until remediation is validated.

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Each ministry's Chief AI Officer (CAIO), with planners, shall conduct use-case risk assessments and determine the risk level (including whether likely high-risk), referring to the High-Risk AI Project Finder (Appendix 1); likely high-risk cases are reported to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board; the CAIO makes the final determination.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Technical report on properties, risks, methods and processes for AI in safety functions, non-AI safety functions protecting AI-controlled equipment, and AI used to develop safety functions; published Jan 2024, 73 pages.

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Discrimination impact assessments could be considered before release; the guideline says the timing and documentation of results and mitigations should be addressed.

framework: ADGM FSRA Supplementary Guidance - Digital Investment Management
requirement_paraphrase: Digital investment managers must document the model's decision logic so outputs are explainable, traceable and repeatable, check data and assumptions stay relevant, and run sufficient, regular testing to show the model meets these principles. For complex models the FSRA may require a third-party audit of performance claims.

framework: SDAIA AI Service Provider Accreditation (National Data Governance Platform service)
requirement_paraphrase: AI software and service providers register, appoint an AI officer, and complete a per-product questionnaire with supporting files on adherence to AI ethics standards; after committee review the product receives an incentive label and the provider an accreditation certificate.

framework: Japan - AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI)
requirement_paraphrase: All actors are to conduct appropriate risk analyses and take countermeasures against identified risks.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: A risk assessment must be done for all AI systems and related assets; risks are tracked in a register with assigned owners.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct adversarial testing at a regular cadence to map and measure GAI risks; evaluate performance in real-world scenarios; verify and document that structured public feedback results are incorporated in deployment go/no-go decisions.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Planned technology-neutral guidance on red teaming of AI systems: terminology, risk and attack vector identification, planning and conducting assessments aligned with 29119, reporting, and lifecycle integration; at stage 20.00 (registered April 2025).

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (v1.5, published 2026-05-20, updated 2026-06-05)
clause_or_page: s.2.3.2 'Before deploying, test agents', case study box 'Google x Singapore Government: Testing computer use agents', p.40 (v1.5)
requirement_paraphrase: Case study (descriptive): Google, CSA, GovTech and IMDA ran a sandbox testing computer-use agents for three potential public-sector uses (automated QA of government digital services, automated AI safety testing of third-party chatbots, social assistance applications). Lessons: use realistic test data and environments; log and evaluate the agent's reasoning at each step; identify use-case-specific attack vectors such as indirect prompt injection; keep humans in the loop during testing. Findings: the agent included extraneous personal details in a significant number of cases and in some instances navigated to arbitrary URLs when instructed by injected content.

framework: China - GB/T 45654-2025 Cybersecurity Technology: Basic Safety Requirements for Generative AI Services (effective 1 Nov 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: All training data is filtered; assessment uses manual samples of at least 4,000 items (qualified rate at least 96%) and technical checks of at least 10% of volume (at least 98%).

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: All proprietary and third-party AI software must undergo formal secure code reviews and automated vulnerability scanning before deployment and during major updates, following recognised frameworks such as OWASP or NIST.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Defines methods for measuring the performance of ML models and algorithms on classification tasks; published 13 Oct 2022, 33 pages; stage 90.92; draft ISO/IEC DIS 4213 would widen scope to regression, clustering and recommendation.

framework: UAE AI Guide (National Program for AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers should test algorithms before field deployment and check training data representativeness for the affected population.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Policy on Use of AI in the Healthcare Sector (Policy/AI/0.9, 30 Apr 2018)
requirement_paraphrase: DoH expects AI tools introduced in Abu Dhabi for healthcare delivery, public health, pharmaceutical production and medical research to be robust, evidenced by certification of the AI software (and of major upgraded versions) from recognised international agencies, compliance with ADSSSA regulations, and auditable validation statements.

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators of AI systems whose cumulative training compute meets a threshold set by Presidential Decree must identify, assess and mitigate risks across the lifecycle, maintain an incident monitoring and response system, and submit results to the Minister.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must consider whether the system is likely to adversely affect persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: For high-risk systems in Annex I Section A products, the provider follows the sectoral conformity assessment procedure, Section 2 requirements form part of it, QMS assessment is added, and notified bodies under sectoral law must apply for AI Act designation by 28 January 2028.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Implementation Guidance 3.1.4 (Change Management and Reporting), printed p.21; 3.2.3 (Patch Management), printed p.24; parent policy statements 2.1.4 (printed p.11) and 2.2.3 (printed p.12)
requirement_paraphrase: Manual changes to AI/ML models, algorithms, training data or configurations should be documented, reviewed, approved and tested in a secure environment before deployment, with a rollback plan where possible; patches and updates should be tested in a controlled environment before production.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: A new conformity assessment is required after a substantial modification; changes pre-determined at the initial assessment for continually learning systems and recorded in the technical documentation are not substantial modifications.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (IMDA / AI Verify Foundation, published 30 May 2024; PDF file dated 19 June 2024)
clause_or_page: Trusted Development and Deployment dimension, 'Evaluation', p.14 (government-transparency sentence in 'Disclosure', p.14)
requirement_paraphrase: Benchmarking and red teaming are the two main evaluation approaches today but fall far short of a robust assessment (front-end focus, missing tools incl. dangerous-capability tests, poor comparability); the framework calls for a more comprehensive, systematic safety evaluation approach that could include a baseline set of required safety tests developed in consultation with policymakers; the adjacent Disclosure text says greater transparency to government will be needed for potentially high-risk models.

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: AI operators should define a suitable fallback plan and test it, including thresholds for acceptable results.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Set of voluntary guidelines for pre-deployment testing of LLM apps for baseline safety and reliability across five risks: hallucination/inaccuracy, bias in decision making, undesirable content, data leakage, and vulnerability to adversarial prompts.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Training, validation and test datasets must reflect the target population's diversity; regular data representativeness audits must be done at defined checkpoints with subgroup gaps flagged; bias detection techniques must be implemented and mitigation traceable.

framework: UK DSIT Introduction to AI assurance (published 2024-02-12)
requirement_paraphrase: Lists a spectrum of assurance mechanisms - risk assessment, impact assessment, bias audit, compliance audit, conformity assessment (often including performance testing), formal verification - to be used in combination across the AI lifecycle, proportionate to risk.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Sandboxes give a controlled environment for development, training, testing and validation under an agreed sandbox plan; authorities give guidance and supervision to identify risks, and on request supply written proof and an exit report which market surveillance authorities and notified bodies must take positively into account.

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends approval processes for high-impact AI before production deployment, ensuring cybersecurity risks are assessed and addressed.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (v1.5, published 2026-05-20, updated 2026-06-05)
clause_or_page: s.2.3.3 'When deploying, continuously monitor and test', case study 'GovTech: Phased rollouts of coding assistants', pp.42-43
requirement_paraphrase: Case study: GovTech (statutory board) rolled out agentic coding assistants (Windsurf, GitHub Copilot Agent Mode from Oct 2025; Claude Code from Apr 2026) after extensive tests on failure and threat vectors such as agent manipulation, hallucination and MCP server compromise and after implementing controls; phase 1 limited to GovTech employees, no MCP access and low-risk systems; before phase 2 (other agencies, then vendors) red teaming was conducted to validate guardrails, with central logging and a sandboxed MCP governance path.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 7.1 / Process 7.1.1, p.71 (technical testing, traditional AI)
requirement_paraphrase: System owner selects fairness metrics for sensitive features and measures disparity of error rates across groups.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation must include comprehensive testing across diverse datasets and contexts to confirm accuracy, safety and efficacy.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Effects should be evaluated in clinically relevant conditions integrated into the clinical workflow, comparing clinicians with and without the device; manufacturers should locally validate devices developed and approved in other jurisdictions.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Overview, PDF p.2 (printed p.2); mapping, date and audiences from https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/tools/ai-verify-testing-framework/
requirement_paraphrase: Process-check framework to assess AI systems against 11 principles (transparency, explainability, reproducibility, safety, security, robustness, fairness, data governance, accountability, human agency and oversight, inclusive growth); each item has outcome, process and evidence, answered Yes/No/N/A with elaboration; mapped to NIST AI RMF, NIST GenAI Profile, Hiroshima Process code of conduct and ISO/IEC 42001.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Implementation Guidance 3.4.4 'Testing and Validation of AI/ML Systems', printed p.36 (parent policy statement 2.4.4, printed p.14)
requirement_paraphrase: The entity should keep a framework for testing and validating AI/ML systems so accuracy, reliability and performance meet defined criteria; all AI/ML systems should be rigorously tested before deployment for functionality, security and resilience, covering varied scenarios and edge cases.

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Define, conduct and report a statistically valid analysis procedure, ideally defined in advance, that accounts for sources of variation and uncertainty and states assumptions.

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Guidelines (Smart Dubai v1.11, English)
requirement_paraphrase: Developers and operators could consider formal procedures such as Discrimination Impact Assessments to help ensure fair decisions.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Examine and document transparency/accountability risks; explain, validate and document the model and interpret output in context; examine and document privacy risk.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems should be tested before deployment and regularly while in operation; measurement should include rigorous software testing and performance assessment with measures of uncertainty, benchmark comparisons and documented reporting of results.

framework: ADGM Office of Data Protection - Guidance on DPR 2021 Part 4 (DPIA)
requirement_paraphrase: A DPIA is required before processing likely to create high risk, and the guidance lists as triggers use of personal data in datasets used to train or refine an AI system (in the specific exception context) and profiling or automated decision-making used to decide access to a service or benefit.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Use use-case-appropriate benchmarks to quantify bias, stereotyping and hateful content, documenting benchmark assumptions and possible train/test contamination; conduct fairness assessments across demographic groups using field testing with sub-groups, red-teaming with counterfactual prompts, and general fairness metrics where outcomes are categorical or numeric.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Risk Management Protocol (ref. as extracted DoH/Protocol/DDGO/RALRM/V1/2025, V1, published and effective Oct 2025, revision Oct 2028)
clause_or_page: s3 Recommended Protocol, Risk Evaluation and Treatment, Step 4 'Control Identification', printed p.6
requirement_paraphrase: Risk controls for AI systems are identified through review of safeguards, gap analysis and stakeholder consultation, and are tested through simulations or pilot studies before full implementation to confirm they reduce risk and support AI safety and reliability.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluate regularly for safety risks; demonstrate that the system to be deployed is safe, residual risk does not exceed tolerance, and it can fail safely, including beyond its knowledge limits.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 5, Build and Validate item 2, p. 22
requirement_paraphrase: Technical robustness requires rigorous testing, validation and re-assessment with oversight controls built into development; system integration test sign-off should involve relevant stakeholders.

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends systematic cybersecurity code review, testing and formal approval of all AI-generated code before use in development, integration or production.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluations must assess the effectiveness of safety mitigations, including under adversarial pressure such as fine-tuning attacks or jailbreaking, and whether mitigations may be circumvented or degrade over time.

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
clause_or_page: AI Safety Institute approach to evaluations (published 2024-02-09), sections 'AISI's approach to evaluations'
requirement_paraphrase: AISI conducts pre-deployment and post-deployment evaluations of advanced AI systems using automated capability assessments, expert red-teaming, human uplift studies and AI agent evaluations, focusing on misuse (chemical/biological, cyber), societal impacts, autonomous systems and safeguards.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: For MDMA the manufacturer is expected to provide technical documentation including product verification and validation; documentation should show verification against design specifications, validation that the device performs as intended, a usability study, and validation of safe performance under normal and reasonably foreseeable abnormal conditions.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers need to show valid clinical association, analytical/technical validation and clinical validation; clinical validation follows analytical validation, applies to all risk classes, and is evaluated before market placement and after; example metrics include sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: The AI Office may conduct evaluations of GPAI models to assess compliance or investigate systemic risks, may appoint independent experts, and may request access via APIs or other means including source code.

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Draft provides voluntary preliminary best practices for automated benchmark evaluations of language models and AI agent systems, in three stages: define objectives, implement/run, analyse/report; scoped to existing benchmarks, not creating new ones.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 2, Deploy and Monitor item 3, p. 17
requirement_paraphrase: The AI system should be tested to ensure the combination of available data does not reveal sensitive data or break anonymity.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems with very high residual risk after controls must be prohibited from deployment.

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators must review in advance whether their AI is high-impact and may ask the Minister to confirm.

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Establish minimum thresholds for performance or assurance criteria and review them as part of deployment approval (go/no-go) policies, procedures and processes.

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, proposed amendments (Annex A 'Proposed Changes' to DIFCA Consultation Paper No. 3, June 2026; draft cover 'Consolidated Version No. 3, in force on [XX 2026]'; NOT enacted as seen on 2026-10-16)
clause_or_page: Proposed Reg. 10.3.1(f) 'Safety', Annex A printed p.13; Consultation Paper para 18(b) and Q2
requirement_paraphrase: Proposed new design concept: a System must be designed, developed and operated with safeguards to identify use of personal data, assess and mitigate risks of harm to individuals, and intended to prevent discriminatory or biased outcomes through appropriate oversight, testing and controls.

framework: China - Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (Order No. 15, in force 15 Aug 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Services with public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capacity must complete a security assessment under national rules and complete algorithm filing under the algorithm recommendation provisions.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Demonstrate that the system to be deployed is valid and reliable; document limits on generalisability beyond the conditions under which it was developed.

framework: Dubai AI Integration Matrix Framework for Government Organizations (Dubai Digital Authority, August 2025, Version 1.0 per front matter; earlier listing date 28 Apr 2026 conflicts)
clause_or_page: Ch. 10.3 (AI Ethics Policy) and 10.2 (Initiative Approval), printed p. 87
requirement_paraphrase: States that every AI initiative under DDA must demonstrate alignment with DDA's ethical principles and undergo rigorous validation for ethical compliance across its lifecycle, and passes a standard approval workflow including technical feasibility, business case, risk evaluation and resource sign-off.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Technical report giving an overview of existing methods for assessing the robustness of neural networks, particularly when conditions change; published 10 Mar 2021, 31 pages.

framework: DHA Artificial Intelligence in the Healthcare Policy (HISHD/PP-09)
clause_or_page: s4.6.10, p.11 of 17 (Minimum acceptable requirements for AI tools)
requirement_paraphrase: AI software and major upgraded versions must comply with all required certification from recognised bodies (text truncated in tool output after 'recognised international or local agencies').

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Data scientists are to test AI systems to assess risks, confirm intended performance and compliance with healthcare and safety regulations, assess robustness, fairness and accuracy, and document metrics and logs; data users identify groups at risk of disparate outcomes and report use of relevant attributes.

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct a cybersecurity risk assessment that classifies AI agents' actions by potential impact, likelihood and reversibility, and apply appropriate safeguards.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Litmus is described as a Singapore government service for testing LLM apps of agencies with 1,600 prompts across security, specialised advice, undesirable and political content; default threshold 95 percent safe responses, adjustable; even a single failure in high-stakes hard-gate cases requires investigation.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Planned specification for quality assessment of prompt-based text-to-text generative AI systems, including safety assessment with red teaming; at stage 20.00 (registered Sept 2025).

framework: Japan - Outline of AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI, 4 Apr 2025; provisional translation)
requirement_paraphrase: AI business users are to understand the precision and risks of AI output and confirm risk factors before use.

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Develop guardrails to detect and prevent malicious input, unauthorised actions and sensitive information disclosure, and ensure they are tested before production use and after material changes.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Ethics > Fairness, bias and discrimination > Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Apply bias mitigation and fairness evaluation across the entire AI project life cycle; comply with human rights law, the Equality Act 2010, the Public Sector Equality Duty and EHRC guidance; review outputs and decisions for bias by measuring results for different groups, including intersectional groups; set up feedback routes for unfair decisions or harmful outputs; evaluate continuously as fairness expectations change.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct security risk assessments per industry standards; release models or systems only after appropriate security checks and evaluation, including benchmarking and security testing before release and verifying model/data signatures and hashes.

framework: Law No. (9) of 2023 Regulating the Operation of Autonomous Vehicles in Dubai
requirement_paraphrase: Technical inspections must be conducted on autonomous vehicles; an AV must pass the technical inspection prescribed by RTA to be licensed; the Director General of RTA sets inspection types, frequency and standards by resolution.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 4.1 / Process 4.1.1, p.29 (technical testing, generative AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Carry out regular safety and harm tests (e.g. hallucination, toxicity) using use-case-appropriate benchmarks and red-teaming, document instructions to red-teamers, test in secure environments at several lifecycle checkpoints and before deployment, have stakeholders decide whether scores are acceptable, and share results.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems rated high risk must undergo conformity assessments both before and after deployment, coordinated with DoH's Data and Digital Governance Office.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Analytical validation should use a large independent reference dataset reflecting the intended purpose and population (prevalence, multi-centre sourcing, demographics, justified size, not publicly available), each requirement applying unless there is sufficient evidence that it need not be met; performance should be shown to generalise through multisite investigation and subgroup analysis, and be tested against a gold standard.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: In addition to internal evaluations, signatories ensure qualified independent external evaluators conduct evaluations unless the model is similarly safe or safer than a reference model or no qualified evaluators can be found despite an early search; external reports or justifications go into the Model Report.

framework: UK Frontier AI Safety Commitments (AI Seoul Summit 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatory organisations commit to assess risks of frontier models across the lifecycle, including before deployment, considering results from internal and external evaluations such as independent third-party evaluators and home governments.

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Guidelines (Smart Dubai v1.11, English)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators should consider working with their vendors (AI developers) to continually monitor system performance.

framework: Smart Dubai AI Ethics Principles & Guidelines (Guidelines changelog to v1.11; v1.6 is the Principles changelog)
requirement_paraphrase: AI developers should consider whether their systems can be expected to perform well on previously unseen data, especially for people under-represented in training data.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: AI services must be secure and resilient and comply with Secure by Design principles and the Government Cyber Security Standard; build safeguards including security testing and, for generative AI, content filtering and validation checks.

framework: Japan AISI - Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety v1.10 (28 Mar 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Defines ten evaluation perspectives: toxic output control; misinformation and manipulation; fairness and inclusion; high-risk/unintended use; privacy; security; explainability; robustness; data quality; verifiability.

framework: China - Provisions on Algorithmic Recommendation Management (in force 1 Mar 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must implement entity responsibility for algorithm security, including algorithm mechanism review and technology ethics review.

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Safety mitigations must be robust under adversarial pressure, and signatories carry out post-market monitoring (feedback channels, incident forms, bug bounties and similar) to inform whether the risk stays acceptable.

framework: Japan - AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI)
requirement_paraphrase: For advanced AI systems, developers are to identify, evaluate and mitigate risks across the lifecycle, including before deployment.

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Guidelines (Smart Dubai v1.11, English)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators should subject AI systems informing significant decisions to quality checks at least as stringent as those applied to a human decision maker.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Fully test the product before deployment, have robust assurance and regular checks of the live tool, and provide ways for users to report issues that prompt human review.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systemic-risk GPAI providers must assess and mitigate systemic risks at Union level, track and report serious incidents to the AI Office, and ensure adequate cybersecurity for the model and its physical infrastructure.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.1.2, printed p.11; Implementation Guidance 3.1.2 (Cyber Risk Management for AI/ML), printed p.19
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must identify, assess and mitigate AI-specific cyber security risks systematically and continuously. Guidance: cyber risk assessments should be run at regular intervals and at key lifecycle stages such as model design, data collection, training and deployment, including risks of cloud AI services that use client data.

framework: UAE AI Adoption Guideline in Government Services
requirement_paraphrase: Once the model is ready, it is evaluated against acceptance criteria to confirm readiness for deployment.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: SFDA is to be informed via GHAD of significant changes within 10 days; the manufacturer shall have QMS procedures for change control, and all changes shall be evaluated, verified and validated under those procedures.

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Run output testing (black-box end-to-end evaluation after components and mitigations are in place, reflecting real user interaction) and component testing (e.g. retrieval step in RAG, filters, system prompt) to locate failure points and catch faults masked by correct outputs.

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Consolidated Version No. 2, Regulation 10 (autonomous and semi-autonomous systems)
requirement_paraphrase: Accountability principle: a System must have mechanisms for responsibility and accountability; these may include internal governance and control frameworks or regular external auditing (examples only).

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: For Annex III points 2 to 8 (critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice/democracy) providers follow the internal-control procedure of Annex VI with no notified body.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Implement post-deployment monitoring plans, including capturing input from users and AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery and change management.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Security > Practical recommendations: 'Applies to generative AI' (public-facing LLM chatbots; no automatic destructive or irreversible actions) and 'Applies to AI' (review enterprise access controls before deploying an AI tool)
requirement_paraphrase: Avoid putting LLM chatbots on public-facing government websites unless the risk of direct prompt injection is acceptable for the use case; prevent generative AI responses from automatically triggering destructive or irreversible actions without human review; review enterprise access controls before deploying AI tools.

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Where independent review is needed, the clinical evaluation should as far as possible be reviewed by someone not significantly involved in development and with nothing to gain, proportionate to risk; an evaluation based on a comparator device must show clinical and technical equivalence including the algorithm.

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Policy on Use of AI in the Healthcare Sector (Policy/AI/0.9, 30 Apr 2018)
requirement_paraphrase: AI used in healthcare activities should have graceful-degradation mechanisms with automatic alerts; should be subject to audits and examination by the technology provider; and healthcare end-users must conduct regular audits of AI functionality and report to DoH as needed.

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Principle 1, Build and Validate item 2, p. 14
requirement_paraphrase: Champion-model selection should include fairness metric assessment, with metrics within a threshold defined earlier for sensitive features; failures should be justified.

framework: US NIST AI RMF Playbook (AIRC; companion to AI RMF 1.0)
requirement_paraphrase: Suggested actions include red-team exercises under adversarial or stress conditions, documenting red-team results, and using separate testing teams (set up under GOVERN) so that decisions about AI systems are independent; assess independence and stature of TEVV actors.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Data protection and privacy > Lawfulness and purpose limitation
requirement_paraphrase: The playbook says that before implementing AI solutions a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) is needed; it cites UK GDPR Art. 35(3)(a) as requiring one where AI involves systematic automated evaluation with significant effects, large-scale special category processing or large-scale public monitoring, notes the ICO also requires one for innovative technology processing personal data, says the DPIA should cover each life-cycle stage including training and testing, and that the ICO must be consulted if high risk cannot be mitigated.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Part 3 will give a methodology for using statistical methods to evaluate neural network robustness; at stage 50.00 (FDIS) with an August 2026 stage date, not shown as published on the page read.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Connect measurement approaches to deployment context, informed by consultation with domain experts and other end users, and document them; inform measurement results on trustworthiness in deployment context and across the AI lifecycle with input from domain experts and relevant AI actors, to validate whether the system performs consistently as intended, and document results.

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.1.3, printed p.11; Implementation Guidance 3.1.3 (AI Supply Chain Security), printed p.20
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must identify, assess and manage cyber risks in the AI/ML supply chain. Guidance: regular security assessments of vendors, developers and other third parties should be run, or independent third-party assurance reports (e.g. SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001) or recognised certifications may be relied on; contracts should cover AI cyber security requirements.
